messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: streaming_push_path 5xx rate spike detected (p95 latency > 1200ms) across prod-usw2. Alert threshold breached.

oncall-ryan: saw it, paging in. looking at graphs now. anyone on call with push path context?

kira: i’m free — i’ve been on the sse mux/workers ques. seeing a big backlog in fanout queue (fanout-12). tokens piling up when sequence length > 512.

megan: confirmed. pushes to clients are stalling; workers show retries and circuit open events. suspecting a downstream client amplification + a buggy consumer reconnect loop.

alec: can we route streaming -> buffered fallback for affected routes briefly? we can do a feature-flag flip to stop live chunking and return full response when ready. that should cut connection churn.

oncall-ryan: agree. propose steps: 1) mute live chunking for push-route v2 (small blast), 2) apply short rate cap on streaming ingress from gw (limit per-api-key 2r/s), 3) watch errors and latencies.

platform-nina: putting a gating flag in console now: `streaming.enabled=false` for routes `push.v2.*` in prod-usw2. rolling to 10%->50%->100% over 2 mins.

megan: can we do immediate global flip? rollout safety is fine here — client churn risk is higher.

platform-nina: i can flip to 100% now. command:

```bash
redwoodctl feature-toggle set --env=prod-usw2 --flag=streaming.enabled --value=false --scope=route:push.v2
```

support-jen: heads-up: customers who expect progressive tokens will see delayed, single-shot responses. please add a note to status page: "Temporarily disabling streaming responses in prod-usw2 to stabilize API latency. Some clients may see delayed completions instead of streamed tokens."

megan: doing the flip now.

platform-nina: flipped to 100% for push.v2 in prod-usw2. rollout finished in ~30s.

alec: applying ingress rate caps on edge: `x-rate-limit: 2/s per api_key` and `burst: 5` for streaming endpoints. pushing policy to gw clusters.

oncall-ryan: monitoring: errors dropped ~55% in 60s, p95 latency improved from 1.3s -> 420ms on worker pools. fanout queue drains slower but steady. good sign.

incident-bot: Note: page escalations paused. Ops channel updated.

megan: support-jen please post to status with impact and expected resolution steps. include: mitigations done, temporary behavior change (no tokenized streaming), and link to client migration doc for fallback handling.

support-jen: status update posted. cc @customers-success.

kira: quick telemetry check: token generation service CPU decreased 28%, network egress from sse cluster down 63%. client reconnect rate fell to baseline.

sre-maya: leaving a note — ensure we have a rollback path: `redwoodctl feature-toggle set --... --value=true` ready. also recommend a slow re-enable with canary to 10% then monitor 5m windows.

alec: i’ll create an automated canary: 10% after 10 minutes if p95 < 600ms and 5xx < 0.5% on push path.

oncall-ryan: handoff in 30m to megan for watch. ryan -> megan.

megan: ack, taking follow-on shift. will keep watch and start canary plan in 10m if metrics stable.

platform-nina: logged change in audit: feature flag flip, ingress policy change, and rate limit applied. linking runbook and timelines.

support-jen: customer impact assessment: we have 12 customers using streaming in prod-usw2. 3 showed transient errors before mitigation; none reported data loss. communications sent to those 12 with instructions to handle buffered responses.

kira: capturing lessons: investigate reconnect storm root cause (likely client lib behavior) and add protective backoff at gateway for repeated reconnects within 30s.

megan: next steps: 1) smoke test canary path when enabled, 2) outreach to top 3 streaming customers to recommend client-side backoff, 3) postmortem draft assigned to kira + ryan + megan.

oncall-ryan: any objections to keeping streaming disabled for a 60m stabilization window?

alec: no objections. sounds safe.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: short-term mitigation applied (streaming disabled for push.v2 prod-usw2), rate limits enforced, monitoring set. Severity: S3 -> reevaluate after stabilization window.

megan: i'll start a calendar block for the 60m watch and ping when we begin canary re-enable.

support-jen: posted customer notes to #customers and created follow-up tickets for client outreach.

sre-maya: quick reminder: ensure logs from mux workers are preserved (S3 prefix `incidents/2319091010`) before any log rotation.

kira: done, logs preserved. also added a short eval harness to simulate reconnect loops.

megan: handoff: taking over active monitoring. ryan, if you spot a regression, ping me directly.

oncall-ryan: will do. thanks team. :thumbsup:

megan: (follow-up) metrics look stable at +30m. scheduling canary re-enable in 10m with rollback trigger points. will update thread.

(End of thread)
